name: Red Linen Bandana
summary: Across Elwynn Forest, Red Linen Bandana marks the Defias Brotherhood. Its cloth hides a wearer’s face and can be put to use by local settlers.

sections.title: Mark of the Defias
sections.body: Across Elwynn Forest, full Defias operatives wear woven red linen bandanas. In Northshire Valley, lower-ranking initiates and common thugs use coarse burlap masks instead. The crimson cloth hides a face and marks allegiance to Edwin VanCleef's rogue fraternity. It also signals their rebellion against Stormwind's crown.

sections.title: Repurposed Cloth
sections.body: Sara Timberlain at the Eastvale Logging Camp asks travelers to gather bandanas from outlaw encampments. Though tied to bandits, the masks are made from respectable linen. After washing and needlework, settlers can turn the cloth into sturdy clothing and bandages for the forest's working folk.

faq.q: Why do the Defias wear red linen bandanas?
faq.answer: Defias operatives wear red linen bandanas to hide their faces and show allegiance to Edwin VanCleef's brotherhood and defiance of Stormwind.

faq.q: How do these differ from the masks worn in Northshire?
faq.answer: Northshire Valley thugs wear coarse burlap masks, while established Defias operatives across Elwynn Forest wear finer red linen.

faq.q: Who wants to collect these bandanas?
faq.answer: Sara Timberlain at the Eastvale Logging Camp wants the bandanas. She washes and unravels the masks to weave practical garments.

faq.q: Which enemies carry red linen bandanas?
faq.answer: Defias operatives across Elwynn Forest carry red linen bandanas, including Defias Bandits, Ambushers, Rogue Wizards, dockworkers, and ringleaders such as Morgan the Collector.

angles.text: In rural Elwynn, weavers can put the linen in bandit masks to use as working clothes.
As a rogue, you know the crimson cloth tied across the lower face as the mark of highwaymen and cutpurses in the woods around the capital.
